summary.headline: GRP Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 94 million (7% margin) from INR 331 million as EPR income, exports and raw-material costs weighed.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income declined 10% YoY to INR 1,450 million, with the prior-year base inflated by INR 305 million of EPR gains versus INR 66 million this quarter. FY26 total income fell about 3% to INR 5,380 million and EBITDA dropped to INR 429 million from INR 694 million, with adjusted PAT of INR 46 million after a INR 14 million Labour Code charge. Export volumes fell about 15% while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, and raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs. Management said the Pyrova (pyrolysis) and rCB platforms are still stabilising, and that the revised pricing from April 2026 passes through the full raw-material impact.

segments.name: Reclaim Rubber (RR)
segments.commentary: Export volumes fell about 15% in FY26 (export revenue down about 11-12%), while domestic revenue grew about 11%; domestic margins run 200-250 bps below export. Management expects the lost US volume to be fully restored in FY27; 38% of capacity has moved to the new process platform, saving about 5% on power.

segments.name: Pyrova Energy (pyrolysis, crumb rubber, rCB)
segments.commentary: Continuous pyrolysis started in H2 FY26 at Solapur; operating above 85% utilisation monthly. Cumulative investment about INR 79 crore to March 2027 target; TPO sales are currently fuel-only, with industrial furnace and petchem approvals still in validation. Recovered carbon black facility (12,000 t) expected in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Non-Reclaim standalone businesses
segments.commentary: Grew about 13% YoY and 22% QoQ in Q4 FY26, mainly from pyrolysis start-up. Custom Die Forms volumes rose 4%; plastics (PP, nylon) faced low-cost Chinese virgin PP imports, hitting packaging margins and volumes. Polymer Composite business was closed, with a INR 79 lakh write-off.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth capex targeted at about INR 90-100 crore, mainly for Pyrova Phase 1b (rCB and additional pyrolysis lines, phased completion by February 2027).
Second new-technology reclaim rubber line to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27 in Solapur, taking capacity from about 350 to about 700 tonnes per month.
Pyrova is expected to deliver high double-digit EBITDA margins; a few hundred bps improvement in RR EBITDA margin is expected; full impact in FY28, with some improvement in FY27.
EPR accrual for the pyrolysis business expected by H1 FY27 once PCB approvals come through, with credits accrued retrospectively.
Revised pricing from April 2026 is said to fully pass through raw-material inflation, subject to current conditions.
Management expects operating leverage to improve progressively in the medium term as the new businesses stabilise.
capex_capacity: Cumulative Pyrova Energy investment about INR 79 crore to March 2026; Phase 1A (15,000 t single-line reactor plus crumb rubber) completed by October 2025 and stabilised in Q4 FY26.
Capex FY24-FY26 about INR 170 crore: roughly 50% Pyrova, 30-35% Reclaim Rubber (capacity and new technology), about 15% other (including solar/wind and an SPV for power offtake in Solapur).
Post-expansion capacity: pyrolysis about 45,000 t (two added reactors), rCB about 12,000 t, crumb rubber about 65,000 t versus over 45,000 t currently.
Solar/wind and renewable projects in Ankleshwar and Panoli expected in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: US tariffs hit about 33% of RR revenues from key US customers and about 44% of associated raw-material margins in FY26; after February revisions the impact moderated to about 41%.
Domestic rubber consumption grew about 4% and reclaim rubber consumption about 7% in FY26; GRP's share in the tyre industry rose.
Raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs; margin erosion was seen in Q2, Q3 and part of Q4 because tyre-company contracts are annual or half-yearly.
Management said the order book is stronger than most of FY26, with North American direct volumes largely recovered but indirect volumes via Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia only partly recovered.
Pyrolysis oil realisations in Q1 FY27 are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026 levels, but road-construction volumes are down because of bitumen shortages from the West Asia conflict.
EPR credits are priced at about the floor of INR 2.52/kg; about 85% of credits are contracted with tyre companies and about 15% sold on the spot market.

qa_highlights.question: How much one-time loss came from Polymer Composite in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Actual write-off was INR 79 lakh; notionally another INR 40-50 lakh could be attributed to the business.

qa_highlights.question: Did pyrolysis oil realisations improve with high crude prices, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefit in March; Q1 FY27 realisations are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026, but road-construction demand is weaker, so volumes are affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery trend in exports and order inflows, and have RM costs stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: North American direct volumes are largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26. Revised pricing from April 2026 captures the full raw-material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capex breakup, and what is the feedback on TPO and the new reclaim technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about 50% Pyrova, 30-35% RR and about 15% other. TPO is in validation for industrial furnaces, with petchem approvals longer. A second new-technology RR line will be added by end Q1 FY27, taking capacity to about 700 t/month from about 350 t/month.

qa_highlights.question: How much EPR income will pyrolysis and rCB generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyrolysis EPR accrual awaits PCB approvals, expected within weeks, with retrospective accrual in Q1 or Q2 FY27. Credits accrue at about 0.8 weightage with about 1.5x conversion; the mix of crumb, char and TPO is not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA margin after Pyrova stabilises, and how will capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyrova expected at high double-digit EBITDA margins, with full impact in FY28. Funding will mix DFI Proparco undrawn limits, internal accruals and possibly unsold EPR credits; serviceability is described as strong.

risks_watch: Pyrova approvals (PCB) for EPR accrual; the timing of catch-up accrual affects H1 FY27 earnings.
Petchem and industrial-furnace TPO approvals are still pending, and oil-price deltas between FO, LSHS and CBFS are unstable.
Debt-to-equity rose to 1.15 from 0.76, and the company is considering debt, accruals or a QIP after the earlier QIP approval lapsed.
Recovery of indirect US-linked volumes via Southeast Asia, and the status of US tariff revisions.
Chinese virgin PP imports continuing to erode recycled PP competitiveness in packaging.
Gross margin of 46% in Q4 versus 54% in FY25; the EBITDA trajectory needs to recover toward FY25 levels.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about a weak FY26 and attributed the decline to tariffs, raw-material inflation and start-up costs, while expressing confidence in the Pyrova and reclaim-rubber expansion. Answers were often evasive on forward margins and petchem pricing, and some questions were repeated or deferred because of line disturbance.
key_quotes: FY '26 represented an important transition year for GRP.
Export volumes for the company declined by about 15%, while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, supported by a proactive market development and selective pricing actions.
As far as the new Reclaim Rubber is concerned, approvals are coming through trickling in slowly, but surely, customers are taking a slow approach in improving or increasing the volumes.
But we are expecting that the Pyrova Energy as a business in itself will be high double-digit EBITDA margins is the expectation.

adds.what: Second new-technology reclaim rubber line in Solapur, taking reclaim capacity from ~350 to ~700 t/month
Pyrova Phase 1b: additional pyrolysis lines (pyrolysis capacity to ~45,000 t) and 12,000 t rCB facility
Recovered carbon black facility (12,000 t) expected in H2 FY27

growth.why: Management guides to FY27 growth capex of INR 90-100 crore, a second reclaim line taking capacity from ~350 to ~700 t/month by end Q1 FY27, and US volume restoration in FY27, but the quarter showed total income down 10% and EBITDA down ~72%, and no revenue growth % was guided.
